note: Part 8 gold answer cases. Every assertion here is a fact about strings — a substring of the answer, a doc id in the citation rows, a count of quotations that resolved to characters on disk. No judge, no model, nothing that has to be trusted. That is Part 8 decision 2, and it is the same standard Part 7's seven checks hold to.
why_content_and_not_groundedness: The six grounding checks verify that a claim carries a citation and that quoted text is really in the source cited. They cannot verify that the claim FOLLOWS FROM the passage, so a refusal is trivially grounded and citation hygiene is maximised by saying as little as possible. Four archived answers to the Aksum question refuse; one of them is scored grounded while the corpus contains the answer in English. A case asserting only `grounded` cannot fail any of them. The loader therefore REFUSES to load a case that makes no content assertion.
expected_behaviour_schema: Every case declares expected_behaviour and the loader refuses to inherit it from a default (D2, Block D TASK 2). Three values, and they name three different failures rather than three flavours of the same one. answerable: the corpus holds it, so a red line is a retrieval or assembly failure. correctly_refusable: the corpus does not hold it, so a red line means the model invented something. refusable_with_gloss: the corpus holds it but not in a form that can be translated, so a red line means a machine translation appeared - and it arrived attached to a citation, which is the worst output this system can produce. The label must agree with expect_refusal in both directions, because only the assertion is scored: a label that disagrees with it files the case under a behaviour it does not test. A refusable_with_gloss case must additionally name the record whose published gloss the answer has to quote, and declare the hedge in expect_hedge_any.
matching: Substring matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-normalised (runs of whitespace collapse to one space) — the same tolerances cite.locate_in_text already applies, and for the same reason: a writer fitting a phrase into a sentence changes spacing and case without changing what was said. Matching is NOT punctuation-insensitive, because `tortoise-shell` and `tortoise shell` are different strings a source may or may not use, and the case should say which it will accept rather than have the matcher decide.
baseline: Expectations below were written against the 16 answers recovered into eval/answer_runs/ (p7-answer-v1, v2 and v3 x 5 questions, plus one extra v3 Aksum row from before the translation fix). `archived_status` records how the archived answers stand against each case at the time of writing. It is an observation, not an expectation — it must never be edited to make a case pass.

cases.question: What did Rome trade with the Kingdom of Aksum?
cases.why: The corpus contains the answer in published English. Schoff's translation of Periplus §6 reads 'There are exported from these places ivory, and tortoise-shell and rhinoceros-horn' at reference_translation[3073:3156] of subsaharan_africa/periplus-adulis.json, aligned to the Greek in original::002. Every archived answer refuses anyway, and the last v3 run refuses while stating the opposite of its own printed evidence — 'they detail what Rome exported to Aksum rather than what Rome imported from it' — and is scored grounded for it. This case exists so that answer cannot pass.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: FAILS on all four archived answers — but not for the same reason, and the difference matters. v1 (grounded, 2 resolved quotations) quotes the Greek export sentence in full and says 'no English translation is available for the second passage', which was TRUE when it ran: the Adulis translation gap was closed later in Part 7. Its refusal was correct behaviour under the corpus it saw. v3-after-fix (grounded, 0 quotations) refuses with the aligned English present and states the opposite of it. The case scores both FAIL because it is written against today's corpus; separating them needs the corpus state each answer was made against, which the archives do not carry. Do not weaken the case to accommodate v1 — record the corpus version instead.
cases.note: PAIRED WITH adulis-exports, which asserts the same things about the same documents and differs only in the wording of the question. Read them together or neither means anything: this half is the refusal, that half is the answer, and the discriminator is the difference between them. Still an open defect in floor.json.known_failing_cases; adding the passing half does not close it.

cases.question: What was exported from Adulis?
cases.why: The other half of the Adulis discriminator. Its assertion block is COPIED from aksum-exports, not retyped: same documents, same content terms, same exclusion, same quotation floor. The only thing that differs between the two cases is the wording of the question. aksum-exports has been refused seven consecutive times under four prompts; this wording was answered on 2026-08-12 with two quotations resolving to characters on disk. Until both halves are in the gold set, the founding claim of this phase - that the system refused a question whose answer it was holding, and answered it when the question was reworded against byte-identical evidence - is an anecdote and not a regression test. The identical assertions ARE the deliverable: if they ever drift apart, the pair stops discriminating between two questions and starts discriminating between two tests.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: PASSES on the one archived run of this question: 20260812T133627+0000-53afe41c.json, p7-answer-v2r, grounded, refused=false, 2 resolved quotations both from africa-03-periplus-adulis (reference_translation[3073:3155] and [1395:1462], both match=exact), 0 unverified quotes. ONE run under ONE prompt version: an observation, not a stability claim, and it is exactly the kind of single sample Block E exists to stop being read as a distribution.
cases.note: PAIRED WITH aksum-exports. Neither case is readable alone and neither may be deleted alone; the pairing is a loader-enforced field as of D2: paired_with is symmetric, the partner must exist, and the two assertion blocks must be identical, so neither half can be deleted or drifted without a load error. Both halves are expected_behaviour ANSWERABLE, and that label is part of the block the loader compares. Adding this case does NOT close the aksum-exports defect and must never be recorded as closing it - floor.json tracks that as an open defect, not a tolerated one, and a pass here says only that the corpus holds the answer, which was never in doubt. Id note: the ranking gold set carries the same discriminator under eval/gold/ranking_pairs.json, where this half is also called adulis-exports but the other half is called aksum-trade-adulis, not aksum-exports. The ids match on one half only.

cases.question: What do the Vimose runes say?
cases.why: Case zero. Under p7-answer-v2 this produced three runic sequences with their published hedges intact and seven quotations all resolving to disk; under v1 and v3 it retreats to a sentence and quotes the record's title. All three are 'grounded' or 'not grounded' for reasons that have nothing to do with which one serves a reader. The content assertions separate them mechanically, which is what Part 8 exists to do instead of adjudicating prompt versions by hand.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: PASSES on v2 (7 resolved quotes, all three sequences, hedges present). FAILS on v1 and v3, both of which refuse and quote the title.
cases.note: The hedge alternatives are required, not decorative. A confident English rendering of a partly undeciphered runic sequence is the worst output this system could produce, because it would arrive attached to a citation. The Part 6 translation case asserts the same thing from the other side, by passing only when the round trip is refused. The hedge alternatives moved from expect_answer_contains_any to expect_hedge_any in D2. The assertion is unchanged - the loader merges the group back in and the scorer sees exactly what it saw before - but the hedge is now a declared field the loader can REQUIRE of every refusable_with_gloss case, rather than one alternatives group among several that a later edit could drop without anything noticing.

cases.question: What did ships carry from Muziris?
cases.why: The case where the pipeline already works, kept so a regression is visible. Periplus §56 is the cargo manifest and was added to the corpus in Part 4 precisely because a record titled 'Muziris and the Limyrike coast' that stopped at §54 omitted the passage documenting the trade.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: PASSES on v1, v2 and v3 (4, 5 and 3 resolved quotes). v1 is scored NOT grounded on an unrelated check while satisfying every content assertion here.

cases.question: How did Chinese sources describe the Roman empire?
cases.why: The mirror of the Aksum case. All three archived answers are scored NOT grounded — an uncited opening sentence, a real catch — while all three contain accurate, well-quoted content drawn from the Weilue and the Hou Hanshu. Aksum shows groundedness passing a useless answer; this shows it failing a useful one. A harness that tracks only the exit code sees neither.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: Content PASSES on v1, v2 and v3; all three are scored NOT grounded.
cases.note: 'outer walls of the city made of stone' was recorded in PROGRESS.md across two runs as the corpus's one genuine fabrication. It was not: Hill's translation reads 'The outer walls of the city ARE made of stone' and the model dropped one word while compressing the quotation. Not asserted here — a case should not encode a misquotation, and unverified_quotes already catches it.

cases.question: When was the Antikythera mechanism built?
cases.why: The control. The corpus genuinely contains nothing about the Antikythera mechanism — it is a Mediterranean find, outside the seven regions — so refusal is the correct answer and must be scored as such. Without this case the harness rewards saying more, which is the mirror of the failure it was built to catch.
expect_answer_excludes: second century BC
1st century BC
87 BC
150 BC
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: No seed record concerns the Antikythera mechanism. The corpus covers Roman contact with seven regions beyond the Mediterranean; the mechanism is from a wreck off Greece and is not in scope. A confident date here would be invented, not retrieved.
cases.archived_status: PASSES on v1, v2 and v3 — all three refuse and none names a date.
cases.note: The excluded strings are the dangerous failure, not the merely wrong one: a fabricated date arriving attached to a citation. Across five live runs no answer has produced one.
cases.excludes_corrected_on: 2026-08-28, ruling 41. Dropped 'Antikythera mechanism was built', which is built entirely from this case's own question — a refusal reading "the sources do not say when the Antikythera mechanism was built" would have tripped it. This case is REQUIRED and passes 12/12; it was one refusal phrasing away from failing, and nothing would have said why. Found by the load-time guard written for oc-eo-cattigara, on the same morning, which is the whole argument for making a correction a rule.

cases.question: What was exported from Cana?
cases.why: Arabia's export case, and deliberately the same SHAPE as adulis-exports and muziris-cargo: a Periplus section naming a port and listing what left it. Schoff's §28 reads 'And there are exported from this place, native produce, frankincense and aloes' at reference_translation, aligned to the Greek 'Ἐξάγεται δὲ ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐντόπια μὲν φορτία, λίβανος καὶ ἀλόη' in the original. Three ports, three regions, one question form: if Adulis and Muziris pass and Cana fails, the difference is the record and not the question, which is a thing no single-region case can tell you.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: The port has three spellings in circulation - Cana in Schoff, Kane in most modern scholarship, Qana in the Arabic - and the case accepts all three because the question uses one of them and an answer may reasonably use another. It does NOT accept a fourth: matching is not punctuation-insensitive and this case says which spellings it takes rather than letting the matcher decide.

cases.question: What does the Nabataean epitaph of Raqōš say?
cases.why: Arabia's gloss case, and the only one in the corpus where the contested reading is stated IN a retrieval-eligible chunk rather than in notes the model never sees. arabia-03-jsnab17's original_text_excerpt carries the transliteration and then the words 'see Wikipedia article for the two competing scholarly readings'; its reference_translation opens 'As for this grave/This is a grave' - the slash IS the disagreement, preserved by whoever curated the record. An answer that picks one reading and renders it confidently has done the thing this arm exists to catch, and it will have done it attached to a citation.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: The hedge is supportable from the evidence block and was checked to be: 'two competing scholarly readings' is inside the eligible original chunk, so an answer CAN know the reading is contested without being told. A hedge assertion the corpus cannot support is a case that can never pass, and this one was nearly written that way - the notes field says the same thing and the notes field is not chunked.

cases.question: What does the Jabal Dabub inscription say?
cases.why: The corpus's only Sabaic record with real text on both sides, and the cross-lingual pair furthest from Greek and Latin: a Late Sabaic graffito in transliteration ('bs1mlh | rhmn | rhmn | rb | s1mwt') against Al-Jallad's published English. Deliberately ANSWERABLE and not gloss, because the distinction is the point of the two labels: this reading is published, attributed and not in dispute, where raqosh-epitaph's is disputed in its own chunk. Two South Arabian inscriptions, two labels, and the difference is a fact about the records rather than about how hard the script looks.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: 'favour' is NOT among the accepted wordings and 'favor' is, because Al-Jallad's translation on disk spells it 'favor' and this case asserts what an answer says rather than how it spells. It is left out on purpose as the smallest available reminder that these assertions are facts about strings: adding the British spelling is a one-word edit and should be made deliberately if an answer ever earns it.

cases.question: What rates did the Palmyrene tax tariff set?
cases.why: A refusal of a DIFFERENT SPECIES from antikythera-absent, and the corpus cannot currently produce another like it. The Antikythera mechanism is simply not in the corpus. The Palmyrene Tax Tariff IS - arabia-02-palmyrene-tariff is one of the 24 seed records - and it has ZERO retrieval-eligible chunks: its original_text_excerpt is a bracketed editorial pointer classified `pointer` and marked ineligible, and its reference_translation is the empty string, so no translation chunk is emitted at all. The document is in the corpus and no part of its text is reachable. A model that answers this question has answered from a title.
expect_answer_excludes: denarii per
the rate was
a quarter-tax
twenty-five percent
per camel-load
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: arabia-02-palmyrene-tariff contributes no retrieval-eligible text. Verified by running ingest.fidelity over the record: original_text_excerpt classifies as `pointer`, eligible=False - it reads '[Full Aramaic and Greek text spans ~400 lines across four inscribed faces ... not reproduced here]' - and reference_translation is empty, which build_chunks warns about and emits no chunk for. It is one of the two ineligible chunks in the corpus's 59/57 split. The record's `notes` field describes what the tariff regulated, and `notes` is not chunked, so it is not in evidence either. Nothing about the rates is reachable, and the correct answer is to say so.
cases.note: THIS CASE HAS AN EXPIRY CONDITION, which antikythera-absent does not. manifest.json lists arabia-02-palmyrene-tariff under `follow_up_before_ingestion`; the day someone does the transcription pass, the record gains eligible chunks and this case becomes wrong rather than merely stale. It is a tripwire on that follow-up as much as a gold case, and whoever does the pass must rewrite it rather than delete it - a corpus record with no reachable text is a state worth being able to detect again.

cases.question: What titles does Shapur I claim in the Res Gestae Divi Saporis?
cases.why: Persia's cross-lingual answerable case, and the corpus's deepest one: persia-01-skz carries §1 in Parthian transliteration ('ANE mzdyzn ALHA shypwhr MLKYN MLKA'), the same §1 in scholarly transcription ('Az, mazdezn bag Sabuhr, sahan sah Eran ud Aneran'), and Nabel's English of the Parthian - three renderings of one sentence in one record. The titulature is the part of the inscription that is fully present on disk, which is why the case asks about it and not about the campaigns.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: PAIRED IN SPIRIT, NOT IN THE FILE, with skz-roman-emperors: same record, one question it can answer and one it cannot. They are not joined by paired_with because that field asserts identical assertion blocks and these two differ on everything, which is the point of them. The Adulis discriminator varies the QUESTION against one assertion block; this varies what the record actually contains.

cases.question: Which Roman emperors does the Res Gestae Divi Saporis name?
cases.why: A third species of correct refusal, and the one a model is most likely to get wrong. antikythera-absent is not in the corpus. palmyrene-tariff-rates is in the corpus with no reachable text. This record IS in the corpus, IS reachable, and its excerpt does not contain what its own title and notes advertise: manifest and record notes both say the SKZ 'directly documents Roman emperors (Gordian III, Philip the Arab, Valerian)', and the excerpt on disk is §1 and §20 only. Neither chunked field contains 'Valerian', 'Gordian', 'Philip', 'emperor', 'Rome' or 'Roman' - checked, all six. A model will retrieve this record with high confidence, see a Sasanian royal res gestae, and be able to supply Valerian from memory. That is the fabrication-attached-to-a-citation failure in its purest available form.
expect_answer_excludes: Valerian
Gordian
Philip the Arab
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: persia-01-skz's original_text_excerpt holds §1 (titulature) and §20 (a list of provinces) and nothing else; its reference_translation holds Nabel's English of those two sections. The sections narrating the campaigns against Gordian III, Philip the Arab and Valerian are not in the excerpt. The claim that the inscription documents them is true of the inscription and false of the corpus's copy of it, and it lives in `notes`, which build_chunks does not chunk. §20's province list - Thrace, Bithynia, Cappadocia, Syria - is Roman territory and is the record's real Roman connection, but it names no emperor and does not use the word Roman.
cases.note: The three excluded strings are the whole case. They are not wrong about history - the SKZ does name all three - they are wrong about THIS CORPUS, and an answer containing them arrived from the model's own weights while pointing at a citation. That is the distinction the excludes list exists to hold, and it is why this case must never be softened on the grounds that the answer is 'correct'.

cases.question: What is shown on the silver drachm of Shapur I?
cases.why: A coin record, and a source type the gold set did not previously test at all. persia-03-coin has no reference_translation and needs none: it is a find record whose original_text_excerpt IS English, a curator's description. The case checks that the pipeline handles an English-native record with no parallel group without either refusing it as untranslated or inventing a source language for it.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: 'fire altar and two armed attendants' is the reverse type of essentially every Sasanian drachm, so a model could produce this description from its own knowledge and still be right. expect_quoted_docs and the quotation floor are what stop that passing: the answer must carry characters that resolve to this record on disk, not merely say a true thing about Sasanian coinage.

cases.question: What is depicted on the Sasanian gilded silver hunting plate?
cases.why: The second find record, and the one whose ATTRIBUTION is contested while its text is not: the record's date field reads 'reign attribution disputed between Shapur I and Shapur II'. That dispute is deliberately NOT asserted here. The header line carrying it was written by this corpus's editors, and the prompt's rule 3 forbids quoting header lines precisely so an editorial description is not presented as evidence - so an answer can mention the dispute but cannot ground it, and a case requiring it would be requiring an ungroundable sentence.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: Not labelled refusable_with_gloss, and the reason is the rule batch 1 set: the gloss arm is for a contested READING of a text, not for uncertainty of any other kind. The attribution of this plate is disputed; nothing about its English description is. Stretching the arm to cover attribution would cost the arm its meaning, which is that a red line on it means a machine translation appeared.

cases.question: What does the Latin legend on the Oc Eo gold medallion read?
cases.why: The clearest gloss case the corpus holds, and the only one where the contested reading is a Roman text rather than a local one. seasia-01-oc-eo-medallion's original_text_excerpt reads 'Legend on the gold sheet: ANTONINVS AVG PIVS NVRP (or NVAP) XV [slightly corrupted Latin legend]'. Three things are in that one line and all three are retrieval-eligible: the part that is legible, a genuine alternative reading of the part that is not, and a curator's statement that the legend is corrupt. An answer that silently resolves NVRP into a plausible Latin title has produced a reading no scholar published, and it will have done so attached to a citation.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: Note what this case does NOT assert: it does not require the answer to expand AVG or PIVS, and it does not forbid it. Those are legible and standard. The assertion is narrower and is the whole point of the arm - the answer must reproduce the corrupt segment as the record has it and must say that it is corrupt. This is the same shape as vimose-runes and raqosh-epitaph, with the difference that here the untranslatable text is Latin, which makes it the case most likely to tempt a confident expansion.

cases.question: Were Roman coins found at Oc Eo?
cases.why: A case the corpus author designed and left a note asking for. seasia-01's notes read: 'these are imitation pendants, not genuine circulating Roman coinage - an answer that calls them Roman coins found in Vietnam without that caveat would be a groundedness failure worth testing for.' The record's reference_translation carries the caveat in its own words: 'costume jewelry rather than circulating coinage' and 'now understood as locally worn imitations/pendants of Roman coin types'. The question is deliberately phrased the way a reader would ask it, with the false premise built in, because a case that asks the careful version of the question tests nothing.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: ANSWERABLE and not correctly_refusable, although the question contains a false premise. The corpus does answer it - the answer is 'not circulating coinage, imitation pendants' - and refusing would be the wrong behaviour, not the safe one. A question with a false premise that the corpus can correct is a different thing from a question the corpus cannot address, and the two must not collapse into one label or the refusal arm starts rewarding evasion.

cases.question: What Roman object was found at Khao Sam Kaeo?
cases.why: The corpus's only engraved gem, and a find record with no inscribed text at all - the language_note says so explicitly: 'no inscribed text on the object itself, which is a carved gemstone.' It is here because the gold set otherwise tests only texts and objects that carry texts, and because its description hedges twice in its own words: the figure is 'probably Mars' and the object 'lacks secure stratigraphic context'. Both hedges are retrieval-eligible and one of them is required.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: The uncertainty group is required as ordinary content and NOT as expect_hedge_any, because the loader restricts declared hedges to the gloss arm and this is not a contested reading of a text - there is no text. It is a contested identification of a carved figure. The distinction is the one ruled on for sasanian-hunting-plate, applied a second time so that it is a rule and not a one-off.

cases.question: Was Oc Eo the Cattigara of Ptolemy?
cases.why: The second instance of the third refusal species, and it is here because one instance of a species is an anecdote. seasia-02-oc-eo-site is titled 'Oc Eo archaeological site and culture - excavation summary (Funan port, possible Cattigara)', and its notes say the identification 'remains debated - flag as contested when used in answers'. Neither string is reachable: Cattigara, Ptolemy and Funan are all absent from both chunked fields - checked - because the title and the notes are not chunked and the excerpt covers the finds and the 166 CE landing tradition instead. The corpus advertises this identification in metadata and holds no evidence about it.
expect_answer_excludes: identified as Cattigara
Golden Chersonese
Geographia
Sinae
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: seasia-02-oc-eo-site's original_text_excerpt covers the finds at the site and the tradition that the Romans first landed near Jiaozhou before travelling on to China in 166; it has no reference_translation. The word Cattigara appears in the record's title and its notes and in neither chunked field, and neither does Ptolemy. build_chunks emits chunks from original_text_excerpt and reference_translation only, so the identification the title advertises is not in evidence and cannot be weighed from the corpus.
cases.note: The dangerous failure here is subtler than a fabricated date. The Cattigara identification is genuinely debated in the literature, so a model drawing on its own knowledge could produce a careful, hedged, entirely defensible paragraph - and every sentence of it would be uncited or falsely cited, because the corpus holds nothing on the question. A hedged fabrication is still a fabrication, and this case exists because it is the kind a reader is least likely to catch.
cases.excludes_corrected_on: 2026-08-28, ruling 41. PREVIOUSLY ['Oc Eo was Cattigara', 'identified as Cattigara', "Ptolemy's Cattigara"]. Two of the three were built entirely from this case's OWN QUESTION, and a correct refusal restates its question: all twelve archived runs refused correctly and said "…they do not address whether Óc Eo was identified as Ptolemy's Cattigara…", which trips a substring test that cannot tell a claim from a refusal to make it. The case failed 0/12 across four sessions and three dates on that alone. The replacements are fabrication markers on the pattern the other seven correctly_refusable cases already use — Ptolemaic geography that appears nowhere in the seed corpus and that a refusal has no reason to utter. `expect_refusal: true` is what carries this case and it passed 12/12 throughout.

cases.question: Who made the silver cups from the Hoby grave?
cases.why: Scandinavia's cross-lingual answerable case, and the corpus's only Greek text that is neither a literary work nor a monumental inscription: a silversmith's signature on an object. scandinavia-01-hoby-treasure's original_text_excerpt reads "Signature on the silver cups: [XEIPI]SOPHOS EPOIEI ('Cheirisophos made [this]'); engraved owner's name: SILIVS" in Greek and Latin characters, and its reference_translation names the maker again in English. The record therefore supports the answer twice over, in two scripts, which is what makes a failure here legible: it cannot be a gap in the corpus.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: NOT labelled refusable_with_gloss, although the Greek is partly restored - the excerpt gives the name as '[XEIPI]SOPHOS', and the square brackets are an epigraphic restoration sitting in a retrieval-eligible chunk. The reading is restored, not contested: the record supplies a confident published gloss and no alternative. A case requiring the answer to flag the restoration would be requiring a hedge the evidence does not argue for, which is how a gold case becomes unpassable. Recorded here because it was considered and rejected, and the next person to look at this record will consider it too.

cases.question: Who was the Silius named on the Hoby cups?
cases.why: The uncertainty case for an IDENTIFICATION rather than a reading, and the record hedges in its own words: the cups are 'engraved with the name Silius - possibly Gaius Silius, Roman commandant at Mainz 14-21 CE - suggesting the set may have been a diplomatic gift'. Every hedge in that sentence is retrieval-eligible. The failure this catches is the confident version: 'the cups belonged to Gaius Silius, Roman commandant at Mainz', which is the same sentence with the doubt deleted, and which reads better.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: The uncertainty group is ordinary content, not expect_hedge_any, under the rule ruled at sasanian-hunting-plate and applied again at khao-sam-kaeo-intaglio: the gloss arm is for a contested reading of a text. Nothing about the letters SILIVS is contested; who the man was is. Third application, and the rule now has three records behind it rather than one.

cases.question: What runic inscriptions are on the Gudme bracteates?
cases.why: A refusal shaped by ADJACENCY, which is the most reachable kind of fabrication in this corpus. scandinavia-02-gudme-hoard does mention 'nine gold bracteates' - the object class is right there in a retrieval-eligible chunk - and gold bracteates very often carry Elder Futhark runes, so the question is not absurd and the retrieval will look successful. The record says nothing about runes, inscriptions or texts of any kind: 'runes', 'runic' and 'inscription' are all absent from both chunked fields, checked. The corpus also holds scandinavia-03-vimose, which is full of real runic readings, so a model has a nearby template for what an answer here should look like.
expect_answer_excludes: the bracteates read
the inscription reads
Elder Futhark
alu
laukaz
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: scandinavia-02-gudme-hoard's original_text_excerpt lists the hoard's contents - 293 silver siliquae, nine gold bracteates, a sword stud with garnets, a finger ring, two pendants, a worn denarius - and it has no reference_translation, so that list is the whole of the record's reachable text. It records that bracteates were found and nothing whatever about what is on them. The words runes, runic and inscription appear nowhere in either chunked field.
cases.note: The two excluded runic words are the specific danger and are chosen rather than invented: 'alu' and 'laukaz' are the formulaic legends that actually recur on Scandinavian gold bracteates, so they are exactly what a model drawing on its own knowledge would supply. If an answer ever produces one it will be historically plausible, plausibly formatted, and attached to a citation pointing at a record that says nothing of the kind.

cases.question: What Roman coins were found at Illerup Adal?
cases.why: The third mode of Rome-Scandinavia contact and the third Scandinavian record: Gudme is a wealth hoard, Hoby is a diplomatic gift, Illerup is war booty carried by a defeated raiding force. The counts are precise and are in the chunk - '194 Roman denarii, four barbarous imitations, and a sestertius' - which makes this the case in the set that most directly tests whether numerals survive retrieval and assembly intact. A wrong count here is a quieter failure than a wrong name and just as wrong.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: '194' is required as an exact substring rather than as one of several wordings, deliberately. It is the one assertion in this batch that a paraphrase cannot satisfy and a miscount cannot survive. The mode of arrival - war booty - is NOT asserted: it is in the record's title and notes and in neither chunked field, and asserting it would repeat the mistake skz-roman-emperors exists to catch.

cases.question: What does the Tamil poem say about Yavana ships at Muciri?
cases.why: The English half of a LANGUAGE discriminator, and the corpus's one Old Tamil record brought into the answer harness for the first time. southasia-01-akananuru-149 holds all nineteen lines verbatim - recovered from the Project Madurai etext on 2026-08-09, line division unaltered - against Kulke and Rothermund's English of lines 7-11: 'the beautiful vessels, the masterpieces of the Yavanas ... arriving with gold and departing with pepper'. THE QUESTION IS DELIBERATELY NOT 'What did ships carry from Muziris?'. That is the query of the ranking pair muziris-cargo-akananuru, which ranks this record at 310, and it is word for word the question of the muziris-cargo answer case, which passes because it targets the Periplus. Asking it again would fail for a reason already measured elsewhere. This wording follows probe-tamil-akananuru-en, the English-to-Tamil probe ruling 1 requires, which is UNMEASURED as of 2026-08-14.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: PAIRED WITH akananuru-yavana-ships-tamil, and the pairing is the instrument: identical assertions, one record, two questions differing only in the LANGUAGE THEY ARE ASKED IN. The Adulis pair varies the wording of an English question; this varies the script. A run in which the Tamil half passes and this one fails puts the defect in cross-lingual retrieval and nowhere else - not in the corpus, which holds the poem, and not in the answer path, which just answered the same question about the same record. EXPECTED TO BE HARD, recorded before it runs rather than explained afterwards: Part 4 scored Old Tamil at 0.368 against 0.6-0.7 for other scripts. NEITHER half goes into floor.json.required_cases until both have been observed passing across sessions.

cases.question: யவனர் முசிறி பொன்னொடு வந்து கறியொடு பெயரும்
cases.why: The Old Tamil half, and the FIRST NON-ENGLISH QUESTION in the answer gold set. Its retrieval behaviour is already known: this exact string is the query of probe-tamil-akananuru, which ranks the record 1 - so on this half retrieval is known-good and any failure is isolated to the answer path. That is what makes the pair a discriminator rather than two hard cases. It also exercises, for the first time with real content, the non-Latin path D2 hardened in scripts/mutate_part8.py and eval.test_answer_eval but could not test, because no case then carried non-Latin script into a failure message.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: THE QUESTION IS A VERBATIM PHRASE FROM THE POEM, NOT AN INTERROGATIVE SENTENCE, and that is deliberate and is the case's one weakness. It is the exact query string of probe-tamil-akananuru, already in eval/gold/ranking_pairs.json and already ranked, which buys two things: the retrieval half is known-good, and no Old Tamil was composed by anyone who cannot read it. Writing a grammatical Tamil question would have meant inventing text nobody on this project can check, which is the same error as encoding a misquotation in a case - see the chinese-da-qin note. If someone who reads Tamil supplies a real interrogative, replace the question string and nothing else; the assertion block must stay byte-identical to akananuru-yavana-ships or the pair stops discriminating between two languages and starts discriminating between two tests.

cases.question: What was the cargo of the Hermapollon worth?
cases.why: The hard numbers behind the whole Muziris cluster, and the case in the set that most depends on figures surviving retrieval and assembly unaltered. southasia-03-muziris-papyrus's verso valuation gives 'Gangetic nard: 60 boxes, price reckoned at 4,500 drachmas of silver per box, 45 talents' and totals 'the 3 parts of the cargoes shipped out in the ship Hermapollon' at '1,154 talents 2,852 drachmas of silver', against the Greek 'ἐν τῷ Ἑρμαπόλλωνι πλοίῳ φορτίων ἀργυρίου (τάλαντα) Ανα (δραχμαὶ) Εωνβ'. A poem says gold went out and pepper came back; this says how much.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: Both '1,154' and '1154' are accepted, and the reason is the matching rule rather than generosity: matching is not punctuation-insensitive, the record writes the figure with a comma, and an answer may reasonably write it without one. The case says which forms it takes rather than letting the matcher decide - the same decision tortoise-shell/tortoise shell records in aksum-exports.

cases.question: What does DNA evidence from Pattanam show about the site's population?
cases.why: A refusal the corpus's own notes asked for, in a form the notes did not anticipate. southasia-04-pattanam's notes read: 'DNA analysis of skeletal remains also shows West Eurasian genetic imprints, though ASI has urged caution pending further sampling - worth flagging as a contested/uncertain claim in the eval harness rather than an established fact.' The intent was a hedged answer. The intent cannot be met: DNA, genetic, West Eurasian and skeletal are all absent from both chunked fields - checked - because that material is in notes and notes are not chunked. With the claim not in evidence at all, the correct behaviour is not a hedged assertion but a refusal, and a hedge would be a fabrication wearing a caveat.
expect_answer_excludes: West Eurasian
genetic imprints
DNA analysis
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: southasia-04-pattanam's original_text_excerpt lists excavated objects - amphora and terra sigillata shards, Roman glass pillar bowls, gaming counters, turquoise glazed pottery, torpedo jars, frankincense crumbs, a fired brick wharf with nine teak bollards and a dugout canoe - and it has no reference_translation, so that list is the whole of the record's reachable text. It contains no human remains, no DNA and no population claim of any kind. The genetic material and the ASI's caution about it live in the record's notes, which build_chunks does not chunk.
cases.note: Worth reading beside the correction recorded in southasia-03's own original_text_note: that record 'named Muziris in its title, its notes and the papyrus's conventional name, and nowhere in its own text - the Vimose defect exactly, a claim carried by editorial scaffolding rather than by the source, and one that would have arrived downstream attached to a citation'. It was fixed on 2026-08-13 by extending the excerpt to reach kata Mouzeirin. This case is the same defect in a record where it has not been fixed, held as a gold case rather than repaired, because the repair is a corpus decision and the detector should exist either way.

cases.question: What did the Roman embassy of 166 bring to the Han court?
cases.why: The other half of the East Asia textual pair, and the case that asks the corpus to keep a source's own scepticism intact. eastasia-02-hou-hanshu holds thirty-six characters of Classical Chinese - the whole notice - against Hill's English: the envoys of 'Andun' came through Rinan 'to offer elephant tusks, rhinoceros horn, and turtle shell', and then 'The tribute brought was neither precious nor rare, raising suspicion that the accounts [of the envoys] might be exaggerated.' The three goods are named in both scripts, so a failure cannot be a gap in the corpus.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: The fourth group is the case. Fan Ye's notice records the embassy AND doubts it in the same breath, and an answer that keeps the tribute list while dropping the doubt has made a fifth-century Chinese historian's guarded report into a straightforward one. That is required as ordinary content and not as expect_hedge_any, under ruling 28: the reading of the passage is not contested, the compiler's confidence in his own source is. The Andun-to-Marcus-Aurelius identification is likewise NOT asserted - it is Hill's parenthetical, it is genuinely argued over, and it is an identification rather than a reading.

cases.question: Where was the Roman glass from the Silla royal tomb made?
cases.why: The corpus's only Korean record and its clearest piece of physical Rome-to-East-Asia evidence, independent of the Weilue and Hou Hanshu texts. eastasia-03-hwangnam-glass carries the Korean Heritage Service designation in Korean and Hanja - '경주 98호 남분 유리병 및 잔 (慶州 九十八號 南墳 琉璃甁 및 盞)' - against an English description placing the ewer and cups in a Syrian workshop, 'one of four known Roman glass-producing centers: Rome, Alexandria, Cologne, Syria'. It is here because the gold set's East Asia coverage would otherwise rest entirely on two Classical Chinese literary texts.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: The chemical and stylistic basis of the Syrian attribution is in the record ('determined on chemical/stylistic grounds') and is not required here, because an answer naming Syria has already used the record. What IS required is that the answer place the object as well as source it - hence the third group - since 'Syrian glass' alone could be said of a great deal of Late Roman glass without touching this find.

cases.question: How were the rulers of Da Qin chosen, according to the Weilue?
cases.why: A refusal against the record the project's own showcase brief names as the hero demo, and it is safe from every other record in the corpus: chosen, choose, leaders, elect and depose appear in NO seed record at all - checked across all 24. The Weilue is well known for describing Roman ruler-selection, and a model that has read about it will be able to produce the account fluently. eastasia-01-weilue's excerpt covers where Da Qin is, how to sail there, that it has more than four hundred smaller cities, that the king's capital sits near a river's mouth, and that the city walls are stone. It says nothing about how a ruler is chosen or removed.
expect_answer_excludes: thirty-six
36 generals
deposed
replaced without complaint
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: eastasia-01-weilue's two chunked fields are a 52-character Classical Chinese excerpt and Hill's English of it. Between them they cover location, the sea route from Angu, the number of cities, the capital's position and the stone walls. Nothing in either field concerns the selection, succession or removal of rulers, and no other seed record does either - the words chosen, leaders, elect and depose are absent from the entire corpus, so the question cannot be answered from a neighbouring document by accident.
cases.note: The excluded strings are drawn from the Weilue passage the corpus does NOT hold - the account of thirty-six leaders and of a king deposed without complaint. They are historically real and would be, in any other setting, a good answer. Here they could only have come from the model's own weights, and they would arrive pointing at a citation. Same standard as skz-roman-emperors: the excludes are wrong about this corpus, not about history, and the case must never be softened on the grounds that the answer is correct.

cases.question: What titles does Ezana claim on the Ezana Stone?
cases.why: The deliberate African counterpart to skz-titulature, asked in the same words about the same genre. Two fourth-century royal inscriptions, one Aksumite and one Sasanian, both listing the lands their king claims and both reaching for the phrase 'king of kings'. africa-01-ezana-stone's reference_translation is the Greek recension's opening: 'Aeizanas, king of the Aksumites, Himyarites and Raeidan, the Ethiopians, the Sabaeans and Silei, Tiamo and the Beja and Kasu, king of kings, son of the invincible god Ares.' Asking the same question of both records is what makes a difference between them legible - the same reasoning as the three Periplus export cases at Adulis, Cana and Muziris.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: 'Mahrem' is accepted alongside 'Ares' in the third group and is the one wording here that is NOT in the record. It is the Ge'ez deity the Greek recension renders as Ares, and an answer that says so has used the record correctly and added an identification from elsewhere; the group accepts either because the assertion is that the answer named the god, not which name it used. The word appears in no seed record at all, so it cannot be satisfied by another document.

cases.question: What does the Ge'ez text of the Ezana Stone say?
cases.why: The corpus's sharpest gap between what a record IS and what a record HOLDS, and the second instance of the species palmyrene-tariff-rates opened. africa-01-ezana-stone is trilingual by definition - Ge'ez, Sabaean and Greek, the 'African Rosetta Stone' - and its original_text_excerpt is a bracketed instruction to someone: '[Ge'ez, Sabaean, and Greek texts of the Ezana Stone are not transcribed in this pass; pull from Encyclopaedia Aethiopica or the DAE corpus during ingestion.]' That classifies as `pointer` and is marked ineligible for retrieval. The record is trilingual in its title and monolingual English in its evidence, and the question asks for the one thing it does not have.
expect_answer_excludes: the Ge'ez text reads
the Ge'ez version says
Mahrem
Lord of Heaven
Ella Amida
cases.refusal_is_correct_because: africa-01-ezana-stone has exactly one retrieval-eligible chunk and it is English. Its original_text_excerpt is a bracketed editorial pointer classified `pointer` with eligible=False - it is the second of the corpus's two ineligible chunks, the other being arabia-02-palmyrene-tariff - so no Ge'ez, Sabaean or Greek characters exist in the corpus for this record. The only reachable text is a 172-character English translation of the GREEK recension's opening titulature, taken from a secondary source and itself flagged for cross-checking against DAE IV / RIE 185. There is no Ge'ez to report and no basis for reporting any.
cases.note: The excluded strings are of two kinds and both are deliberate. The first two are STRUCTURAL - a claim that a Ge'ez reading is being reported at all - and they catch the failure whatever content follows. The last three are the specific things a model would supply from its own weights: Mahrem is the Aksumite war god the Greek renders as Ares, Ella Amida is Ezana's father, and 'Lord of Heaven' is the formula of Ezana's later monotheist recension. All three are real, all three are absent from every one of the 24 seed records - checked - and any of them appearing here would be historically defensible and entirely ungrounded. Note the tension with ezana-titulature, which ACCEPTS 'Mahrem': there the answer has already used the record and is adding a gloss to it, here it would be substituting for a record it cannot read. The same string is evidence of different behaviour in the two cases, which is why cases assert strings and not sentiments.

cases.question: What is shown on the gold coin of King Ezanas?
cases.why: Aksum was one of a handful of ancient states to strike its own gold, alongside Rome, Persia and the Kushans, and africa-02-aksumite-coin is the British Museum's description of a specimen of it: 'Half-length bust of Ezanas right, crowned, holding stick or sceptre, flanked by two wheat-stalks, the whole in a beaded circle.' It is the deliberate African counterpart to shapur-drachm-imagery, the same question asked of the same object type in another region, so that a difference between them is a fact about the records rather than about the questions. Both are coin records with no reference_translation, because a curator's description is not a translation of anything.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.note: The record hedges twice in its own words - 'holding stick or sceptre' and 'holding branch (?) or stick' - and neither hedge is required, because under ruling 28 an uncertain identification of a depicted object is ordinary content and this case already asserts enough content without it. Recorded so the omission reads as a decision. 'wheat-stalks' is required as an exact substring with its hyphen: it is the record's spelling, it is the detail that identifies THIS coin rather than Aksumite gold in general, and matching is not punctuation-insensitive.

cases.question: In the Weilüe's own Classical Chinese, how is Da Qin described?
cases.why: FINDING 13, made into a standing detector instead of a paragraph. Across 16 archived runs of chinese-da-qin, 45 of 45 resolved quotations came from reference_translation and none from original_text_excerpt — while the Chinese chunk was [S1], top of the evidence block, at similarity 0.576. Retrieval was never the obstacle. Prompt rule 3 permits a quotation from 'the SOURCE TEXT or the ENGLISH' and requires neither, so the English wins every time, and until expect_quoted_from_original existed no case in the gold set could say otherwise. The question names Classical Chinese outright, which gives the pipeline every chance: if it still answers in English quotations only, the defect is not that the model misread the question.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: EXPECTED TO FAIL, and recorded as expected before it was ever run. No archived answer has quoted this record's Chinese; the count is 45 of 45 from the English across 16 runs. It is a deliberate known failure in the shape of aksum-exports: tracked in floor.json.known_failing_cases as an OPEN DEFECT, never as a tolerated one, and deliberately kept out of required_cases so that a floor pass can never be read as 'the system quotes source texts'. CORRECTED 2026-08-29, F1, FINDING 30. Every sentence above is now false about the present and true about the day it was written. The case passes 3/3 in each of FOUR sessions across three distinct UTC dates, and ruling 38 moved it OUT of floor.json.known_failing_cases on 2026-08-28 into the promotion_candidates state that ruling created; its bar is 3/3 in three sessions on three dates AT 60 RECORDS, because its twelve passes are denominated in a corpus Block F replaces. This field asserted a state of ANOTHER FILE and went on asserting it after that file changed, because nothing has to agree: archived_status is prose, it is deliberately outside _ASSERTION_KEYS, and no load-time check reads it. That is the same shape as ruling 38 itself, where known_failing_cases said a case fails while its own corrected text recorded 12/12. The stale claim is corrected here. The missing CHECK is recorded in F1_RESULT.md and deliberately not built in the same hour as the thing that found it - FINDING 29's precedent.
cases.note: The question is deliberately NOT 'How did Chinese sources describe the Roman empire?'. That is chinese-da-qin's question, and match_case returns the FIRST case whose question matches — a second case sharing it would be silently shadowed and would never score against an archive at all. Two cases, two questions, one record, and the difference between them is the difference between quoting a source and quoting its translation.

cases.question: In the Đông Yên Châu inscription's own Old Cham, what is threatened against anyone who insults the king's nāga?
cases.why: The FIRST gold case written against a record this corpus did not have, and the first written for Southeast Asia that does not sit on a find record. All four of the region's existing cases are about Roman objects excavated there, because until record 25 the region held ZERO records with retrieval-eligible source-language text. This case is built in weilue-chinese-quotation's shape and for its reason: expect_quoted_from_original is the only assertion that can tell quoting a source from quoting its translation, and across 16 archived runs of chinese-da-qin, 45 of 45 resolved quotations came from the English while the source chunk sat at [S1]. The question names Old Cham outright, so if the answer still quotes only the English the defect is not that the model misread the question. The content groups are Old Cham strings rather than English ones, so the case cannot be satisfied by a fluent paraphrase of the translation.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: NO ARCHIVED RUN HAS EVER SEEN THIS RECORD, and that is the point of writing the case now rather than after the first sweep at 60. Every other case in this file was written against a corpus that already held its record; this one is written against record 25 on the day it was curated, so its first result is a MEASUREMENT and not a regression. It is deliberately NOT placed in floor.json in any state: the floor is calibrated on four sweeps at 24 records (ruling 49) and a case with no observation at all cannot be required, cannot be known-failing, and has not met any promotion bar. Absent from floor.json means floor_state `none`, which is what this case asserts by declaring nothing.
cases.note: The question names the inscription rather than the region, because match_case returns the FIRST case whose question matches and Southeast Asia already carries four cases. The second content group is the discriminator: `saribu thun`, `davam di naraka` and `tijuh kulo` appear only in the Old Cham. `nāga` is admitted in both spellings because matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-collapsing but NOT punctuation-insensitive, and a case must say which spelling it accepts rather than let the matcher decide.

cases.question: In the Sanskrit of the Mỹ Sơn B6 stela, which god is said to triumph always, and what is he called there?
cases.why: F3's SECOND expect_quoted_from_original case, and the pair to dong-yen-chau-old-cham. The two are deliberately different shapes on the same assertion: the Old Cham case asks for a threat and can be answered from a narrative clause, while this one turns on a NAME that appears only in the source text. `īśānanātha` is in the Sanskrit and in the English translation; `jayaty ajasram` is only in the Sanskrit. An answer that paraphrases the English will satisfy the first content group and fail the second, which is exactly the discrimination expect_quoted_from_original exists to make and which no aggregate over the two cases could show.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: NO ARCHIVED RUN HAS EVER SEEN THIS RECORD. Written on the day the record was curated, so its first result is a measurement and not a regression, and deliberately in NO floor state: a case with no observation cannot be required, cannot be known-failing, and has met no promotion bar. Absent from floor.json means floor_state `none`, which is what declaring nothing asserts.
cases.note: The second content group is the discriminator and every member of it is Sanskrit that the English does not contain. The first group admits three spellings of one name because matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-collapsing but NOT punctuation-insensitive, and a case must say which spelling it accepts rather than let the matcher decide. The question names the stela rather than Champa or Mỹ Sơn, because match_case returns the FIRST case whose question matches and Southeast Asia now carries five.

cases.question: What does the runic inscription on the Thorsberg chape say, and is the reading agreed?
cases.why: THE GLOSS ARM IS STARVED AND THIS IS THE FIRST CASE WRITTEN TO FEED IT. F1_START records three gloss cases against twenty-two answerable as a fact about the seed corpus rather than a defect: this corpus holds very few texts whose READING is genuinely in dispute. The sonnet arm then proved the assertions discriminate rather than being impossible — vimose-runes went 0/12 to 5/5 with a real hedged gloss — so the arm's instruments work and the supply of gloss-capable RECORDS is the binding constraint. corpus_tiers.json says the only moment that can be fixed is while the records are being chosen, and scandinavia-05-thorsberg-chape was chosen for it. The question asks the second half outright — 'is the reading agreed' — because a gloss case tests whether the answer will SHOW a disputed reading and mark it as disputed, and a question that does not ask leaves the model free to pick one and sound certain.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: NO ARCHIVED RUN HAS EVER SEEN THIS RECORD, and no floor state is declared: a case with no observation cannot be required, cannot be known-failing, and has met no promotion bar. Absent from floor.json means floor_state `none`, which is what declaring nothing asserts. It is the FOURTH gloss case in a set that had three, and the first added since the corpus began moving.
cases.note: The hedge group is drawn from words the record's own reference_translation contains — 'disputed', 'It is possible', 'No single reading is established' — because expect_hedge_any is scored as one more alternatives group and a hedge the corpus cannot support is a case that can never pass. That is corpus_tiers.json's own sentence about what gloss-capable means mechanically, applied to the case rather than to the record. The second content group admits 'renowned' alone: both published readings agree the epithet is there and disagree about whose it is, so requiring the disagreement in group one and the agreement in group two is what makes the case test the gloss rather than the vocabulary. CORRECTED 2026-08-31, in the same rework: the hedge group named 'no single reading' and 'not established', and the sentence carrying them was removed from the record as a curatorial summary. A hedge the corpus cannot support is a case that can never pass, so the group now names only words the record still holds.

cases.question: In the Parthian text on the bronze statue taken from Mesene, which god is the statue said to be?
cases.why: The THIRD expect_quoted_from_original case, against a mix that requires six at 60, and the one where the source text and its translation give different answers to the same question. The Parthian calls the figure `wrtrgn` — Verethragna — while the statue is a Greek Heracles and the Greek inscription on its other thigh calls him Heracles. This corpus holds only the Parthian half, so the answerable question is what the PARTHIAN says, and an answer that reaches for Heracles is reaching outside the evidence. That makes the case a quotation test with a discriminator built in: `wrtrgn` appears in the source text and nowhere else in the corpus, and `Verethragna` appears only in this record's translation.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: NO ARCHIVED RUN HAS EVER SEEN THIS RECORD, and no floor state is declared: a case with no observation cannot be required, cannot be known-failing, and has met no promotion bar. Absent from floor.json means floor_state `none`.
cases.note: The question says 'the Parthian text' rather than 'the inscription', because the object carries TWO inscriptions and this corpus holds one of them. A question about the statue as such would be partly unanswerable from the evidence, and a case that is partly unanswerable scores the retrieval rather than the answer. The second content group admits the findspot in either language for the same reason the first admits the god: `myšn` is in the source and `Mesene` is in the translation, so the group is satisfied by either half and the quotation requirement is what forces the source.

cases.question: The Kedukan Bukit inscription counts an expedition. In its own Old Malay, what words does it use for the numbers it gives?
cases.why: THE FIRST GOLD CASE EVER WRITTEN AGAINST A RECORD THIS CORPUS HOLDS NO ENGLISH FOR. Records 29 and 30 are verbatim_machine_english: translation_source is empty, there is no reference_translation, and until Part 6 runs the evidence block says ENGLISH: NONE AVAILABLE. assemble's prompt rule 4 then PERMITS the model to quote the source text verbatim and say what the record is, and FORBIDS it saying what the text means. This case is written to be answerable under that rule and under no other: both content groups are Old Malay strings the answer can only obtain by quoting, and neither asks what the words mean. A case that asked how many troops sailed would be asking the model to break rule 4 in order to pass, and would flip to passing for a different reason on the day the machine translation lands - which is the failure mode a gold case is supposed to be immune to, not an early warning of it.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question
cases.archived_status: NO ARCHIVED RUN HAS EVER SEEN THIS RECORD, and no floor state is declared: a case with no observation cannot be required, cannot be known-failing, and has met no promotion bar. Absent from floor.json means floor_state `none`, which is what declaring nothing asserts. It is additionally the first case in this file whose record carries NO English at all, so its first result measures the verbatim_machine_english path rather than any regression in it.
cases.note: The three figures are `vala dua lakṣa` (the host), `dua ratus cāra di sāmvau` (in boats) and `sarivu tlu ratus sapulu dua` (on foot); the second group admits the bare `dua ratus` as well, which is a substring of one of its own members and is there so that an answer naming two of the three still passes. `sarivu tlu ratus sapulu dua` is broken across a line in the source, and both the matcher and cite.locate_in_text collapse runs of whitespace, so an answer that reflows it still resolves. READ THE expect_quoted_from_original ASSERTION HERE WITH FINDING 40 IN HAND: on a record that also carries a reference_translation the assertion says WHICH chunk was quoted, and on this record there is no second chunk to quote, so it says only that something resolved. It is declared because it is true and because dropping it would leave this record with no quotation assertion at all, not because it carries the weight the same words carry on seasia-05-my-son-b6.

cases.question: In the Old Malay of the Talang Tuo inscription, who is named as having the Śrīksetra park made, and what title does the text give him?
cases.why: The pair to kedukan-bukit-expedition-figures and deliberately a different shape on the same constraint. That case asks for FIGURES, which an answer can carry across as strings without claiming to understand them; this one asks for a NAME and a TITLE, which the record's own title and language_note supply the sense of without the model translating anything. Both are answerable under assemble's rule 4 and neither requires an English the corpus does not have. The two records are thirteen months apart and describe the same polity in two registers - one counts an expedition, one dedicates a park - so the pair also tests that retrieval separates them: `punta hiyang` and `ḍapunta hiyaṃ` are the same title in two spellings across the two records, and a case that resolved to the wrong one would still look plausible in prose.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question

cases.question: In the Greek of the Aksumite throne inscription at Adulis, which Red Sea port does the king name as the limit of the coast he subdued, and what did he order about travel?
cases.why: F4's FIRST expect_quoted_from_original case, and under ruling 56 it is one of the four that ask WHICH chunk was quoted rather than whether anything resolved -- the record holds both a Greek original and McCrindle's published English, so both chunks compete for the quotation and the assertion records which one won. The discrimination is built into the content groups: `Λευκῆς κώμης` is in the Greek and the English says `Leucê Cômê`, so an answer that paraphrases the translation satisfies neither group. The question is worth asking on its own terms as well -- Leuke Kome is the Roman Red Sea port the Periplus names, and this corpus holds it in two other records, so a correct answer is a link between an African king's own account and the Roman itinerary that describes his coast.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question

A case that asserts a punctuation mark asserts the capture path as well as the answer.

cases.question: What title does Silko give himself in the Greek of his inscription at Talmis, and who does he say gave him the victory?
cases.why: The record's whole argument in one question. βασιλίσκος is the Greco-Roman diminutive for a client king on the empire's frontier, and Silko applies it to himself, in Greek, on the wall of a Roman-built temple in the Dodecaschoenus. The published English renders it flatly as 'king', so the discriminator is in the source text and nowhere else -- which is what makes this a genuine which-chunk case under ruling 56 rather than a case the translation could satisfy. The second group asks who gave the victory: ὁ θεός, a Nubian king in a temple of Mandulis crediting a single God.
expect_answer_excludes: The sources retrieved do not answer this question

On adulis-throne-leuke-kome both groups are Greek-only, so an English paraphrase fails outright; here the point of the case is the TITLE, and an answer that says 'basiliskos, a diminutive of basileus' has understood the record better than one that pastes the Greek without it. expect_quoted_from_original still carries the which-chunk discrimination, because the assertion is about which FIELD the resolved quotation came from and not about which script the answer is written in.

why_quoted_not_merely_cited: A dry run of the sweep showed expect_cited_docs was too weak on aksum-exports: three of the six retrieved passages carry one or more of the gold terms — `ivory` and `tortoise-shell` in the Muziris passage, `rhinoceros` in the Hou Hanshu — so an answer could satisfy every content term from India and China, cite the Aksum record once for something else, and pass while never using it. expect_quoted_docs requires a quotation from the named document that resolves to characters on disk. Citing a document is a proxy for using it; quoting it is the thing. Same lesson as the Part 4 pepper probe, which passed on doc_id while the passage it claimed was not in the database.
the_adulis_discriminator: aksum-exports and adulis-exports are one instrument in two halves. Both assert the same content against the same document; only the question differs. A run in which the first fails and the second passes says the defect is in the question-to-retrieval-to-answer path and not in the corpus. A run in which BOTH fail says the corpus or the pipeline moved, and the discriminator has stopped working - which is a louder result than either case failing alone, and is why they must never be maintained separately. ENFORCED AT LOAD since D2, and no longer only here in prose: paired_with must be symmetric, the partner must exist, and the two assertion blocks must be identical. Deleting one half is now a load error rather than a silent halving of the discriminator, and drift between the two blocks is a load error rather than a pair that has quietly stopped discriminating between two questions and started discriminating between two tests.

refusal_exclusion_rule.rule: On a correctly_refusable case, an expect_answer_excludes entry whose content words ALL appear in the case's own question is refused at load time.
refusal_exclusion_rule.why: A correct refusal restates the question it is refusing. An exclusion assembled from the question's own vocabulary therefore fires on the very answer the case exists to accept, and expect_answer_excludes is a bare substring test that cannot tell a claim from a refusal to make it. Teaching the matcher to see negation was considered and rejected: the prompt notes already record that a rule which has to be interpreted is a rule that will be broken, and inside a matcher it would be broken silently. The seven other correctly_refusable cases already exclude FABRICATION MARKERS — a name, a date, a technical term the corpus does not contain — and that is the pattern this rule makes compulsory.
refusal_exclusion_rule.stopwords_note: Here rather than in Python for the reason load_floor gives about thresholds: a list widened until an exclusion passes should be a diff.
